summary: The random-coloring proof yields ||ell_I||^2 ||ell_J||^2 >= L(ell)/4 and hence ||ell_I|| ||ell_J|| >= sqrt(W2)/(4|a|) in the leakage branch. It does not imply that each bank norm separately is >= sqrt(W2)/(4|a|). After orienting the larger bank as J, the valid individual consequence is ||ell_J|| >= W2^(1/4)/(2|a|^(1/2)). At the exact-null endpoint the product constant improves to sqrt(W2)/(2|a|), hence the larger bank is >= W2^(1/4)/(sqrt(2)|a|^(1/2)). The partner's exact determinant identity, leakage/curvature dichotomy, and random-coloring expectation remain valid.
